title: Exactly-Once Processing in Kafka
description: Implement idempotent producers, transactions, and exactly-once semantics in Kafka.

data.text: Exactly-once semantics (EOS) ensure each message is processed exactly once, even when failures or retries occur. Kafka achieves EOS through idempotent producers, atomic transactions, and transactional offset commits. Together, these mechanisms eliminate duplicate and lost messages in complex pipelines.

By default, a Kafka producer assigns a random sequence number per message. On retry, the broker may reject duplicates because it sees a different sequence number for the same partition. Enabling idempotence assigns a persistent producer ID (PID) and monotonically increasing sequence numbers, allowing the broker to deduplicate retries automatically.

data.title: Idempotent Producer in C#
data.content: Configuring an idempotent producer with Confluent.Kafka to prevent duplicates on retry.

data.text: Transactions extend idempotence to multiple partitions and topics. A transactional producer writes to several partitions atomically, so either all messages are visible or none are. This is critical for read-process-write patterns where a consumer reads from one topic, processes the data, and writes results to another.

data.title: Transactional Producer in C#
data.content: Writing to multiple topics atomically using Confluent.Kafka transactions.

data.text: To participate in exactly-once pipelines, consumers must read committed messages only and commit their offsets within the same transaction as any output they produce. The `isolation.level=read_committed` setting ensures the consumer sees only messages from completed transactions.

data.content: Consuming committed messages and producing transactional output with KafkaJS.

data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Producer
    participant B as Kafka Broker
    participant C as Consumer

    P->>B: Init Transactions
    P->>B: Begin Transaction
    P->>B: Produce Message (tx-id)
    P->>B: Commit Transaction
    B->>C: Poll (read_committed)
    C->>C: Process Message
    C->>B: Send Output + Commit Offset (in transaction)
    B->>C: Transaction Committed
data.caption: End-to-end exactly-once flow with transactions

data.title: Performance Trade-off
data.text: Exactly-once semantics add latency because transactions require extra coordination with the broker. For workloads where occasional duplicates are acceptable, idempotent producers without transactions may provide better throughput.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Idempotent producers use PIDs and sequence numbers to deduplicate retries.
Transactions atomically write to multiple partitions and topics.
Consumers must set `isolation.level=read_committed` to participate in EOS.
Use EOS when duplicate or lost messages are unacceptable, such as in financial systems.
data.takeaway: Exactly-once processing turns Kafka into a reliable backbone for critical data pipelines.
